_doc: Diagnostic: does the cardinality cliff exist in MEMORY durability mode too? Memory mode (--durability memory) skips the WAL + all per-append fsync, but STILL writes each append into the per-stream data file (page cache) for reads. So if memory mode ALSO cliffs at high cardinality, the cause is the per-stream data files / N-inode writeback, not the WAL/fsync path — which points at the log-structured store. If memory mode is FLAT while wal cliffs, the cause is WAL durability. Local kind, relative signal. wal arm uses syncfs (best current wal). Capture SRV_STATS (svc_us/applock_us/durwait_us) from the server pod during the 50k cells for the time breakdown.
